content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. Type checking passes for it, but I didn't run any behaviour comparison against the original.

- **`byId`:** it now uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`, with the same `(row) => row.id` callback.
- **`totalAge`:** it now uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`. The core `sumBy` doesn't accept the `'age'` string shorthand, so the call is `sumBy(rows, (row) => row.age)`.
- **`isBlank`:** the core `es-toolkit` has no equivalent of lodash's `isEmpty`, only `isEmptyObject`, which covers plain objects and not strings or arrays. So `isBlank` uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`, which follows lodash's semantics. That covers the whole input range: `null`, booleans and integers give `true`, and strings, arrays and objects give `true` only when empty.
- **No lodash left:** every call has an `es-toolkit` replacement, so the file has no lodash import. The exported signatures, `Row` and `Config` are unchanged.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 606 bytes (min+gzip) and 95 bytes of own code. Importing all three functions from `es-toolkit/compat` instead came to 3404 bytes, so I kept the mixed imports.

I couldn't size or type-check the original `src/module.ts`. It fails to resolve `lodash/*` because lodash isn't installed, so I have no baseline for the own-code allowance.
